speaker: SFX
text: SCENE ONE — 7:06 A.M. A bus shelter. Rain ticks on metal. Someone struggles to close a broken umbrella.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: By seven in the morning, Teresa has already heard four different versions of the truth. None of them were told in the same language. The first came from a voice note sent to the wrong neighborhood group.

speaker: LUPE
text: Attention, residents. At nine, a person from the county will be at the building. The message says the court has made its decision. Repeat: made its decision. I am wearing lipstick suitable for an emergency.

speaker: TERESA
text: Lupe, who sent that?

speaker: LUPE
text: An anonymous woman who says her cousin knows a clerk. You cannot get more official than that without a seal.

speaker: TERESA
text: You can. You can get an actual notice. Also, your voice note says “the court has made its decision,” but the screenshot says “a hearing has been scheduled.”

speaker: LUPE
text: A small difference.

speaker: TERESA
text: A different legal event. A hearing is a chance for people to be heard. A decision is a result. We can’t turn one into the other because the group chat is impatient.

speaker: LUPE
text: Fine. I will post a correction.

speaker: SFX
text: A rapid cascade of message notification tones.

speaker: LUPE
text: The correction now has seventeen reactions, including a pineapple. Someone has asked whether this means they should bring a lawyer, a translator, or chairs.

speaker: TERESA
text: I can tell them where the court explains interpreter access. I can’t tell them what legal decision to make. And I haven’t seen the full notice.

speaker: SFX
text: Bus air brakes. Doors open.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Teresa boards a bus carrying two folders, one sandwich, and a professional rule that she has come to fear more than a difficult word: never improve someone else’s story.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE TWO — 9:40 A.M. An interpreter training room. Chairs scrape. A clock ticks.

speaker: TRAINER
text: Today's simulation is not about being eloquent. It is about being accurate under social pressure. You are not the witness. You are not the judge. You are the interpreter.

speaker: ACTOR ONE
text: I think I saw a man at the entrance. I might recognize his jacket. I couldn't tell whether he was carrying anything.

speaker: ACTOR TWO, AS NOVICE INTERPRETER
text: Vi al hombre en la entrada. Reconozco su chaqueta. Llevaba algo.

speaker: SFX
text: The room goes quiet.

speaker: TRAINER
text: Teresa, what happened?

speaker: TERESA
text: The interpretation upgraded three uncertainties into facts. “I think” disappeared. “Might recognize” became “recognize.” “Couldn't tell whether” became “was carrying.”

speaker: ACTOR TWO
text: It sounded awkward with so many maybes.

speaker: TERESA
text: The witness sounded uncertain. That awkwardness belongs to the witness. We can't polish it away.

speaker: TRAINER
text: Exactly. Your job is not to make testimony persuasive. Try again and keep the degree of certainty.

speaker: ACTOR TWO
text: Creo que vi a un hombre en la entrada. Tal vez reconocería su chaqueta. No pude distinguir si llevaba algo.

speaker: TRAINER
text: Better. We can discuss regional phrasing, but the uncertainty and limits of observation survived. Now a medical conversation. New actors.

speaker: ACTOR THREE, AS CLINICIAN
text: Did the pressure start before you took the medicine or after?

speaker: ACTOR FOUR, AS PATIENT
text: It started before. I took the medicine because I felt that pressure. I don't know if it helped.

speaker: ACTOR TWO, AS NOVICE
text: Empezó después de tomar la medicina. La tomó y se sintió mejor.

speaker: TERESA
text: That is a different history. We changed the sequence and invented an improvement.

speaker: ACTOR TWO
text: I heard “took the medicine” and “pressure.”

speaker: TERESA
text: Hearing the nouns wasn't enough. “Before” carried the timeline; “I don't know” carried the uncertainty. The big words weren't the dangerous part.

speaker: SFX
text: Someone taps the desk twice, like a tiny gavel.

speaker: TRAINER
text: A useful principle: if you didn't understand something, make the interpreting difficulty transparent and request clarification. Don't quietly fill the gap.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE THREE — 12:25 P.M. A café. Cups clink. A small radio plays a scratchy bolero.

speaker: LUPE
text: I have a question. If the words are so fragile, why do people speak so fast?

speaker: TERESA
text: Because they don't know they're entering someone else's future.

speaker: LUPE
text: Very dramatic. You should write telenovelas.

speaker: MARTA
text: I brought the actual notice. I want help understanding what it says, not deciding what to do. Can you read the title aloud?

speaker: TERESA
text: “Notice of hearing.” It names a date and a place. That doesn't tell us what the outcome will be. For the specific legal meaning and your options, ask the court or a qualified legal advisor. The court should be able to explain how to request language assistance.

speaker: MARTA
text: Then the anonymous message that said I already lost my home was wrong?

speaker: TERESA
text: I can't establish the legal status from a group rumor. I can say that the screenshot was misquoted. The document says “hearing,” not “judgment.”

speaker: LUPE
text: Which means we need to apologize to everyone I told to pack their lamps.

speaker: MARTA
text: Especially the woman who already sold her lamp.

speaker: SFX
text: A laugh, then the radio cuts out.

speaker: SFX
text: SCENE FOUR — 6:10 P.M. Teresa's kitchen. A phone vibrates on the table.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: At home, Teresa takes off her shoes and plays the training recording one more time. She has missed a different little word this time. The patient said the pressure started *before*. The trainee said *after*. Without that one bridge between events, the story crosses to the wrong bank.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: LUPE [VOICE NOTE]: I have fixed the post. I wrote: “A hearing was scheduled. No decision has been confirmed in the information we saw.” I also removed the pineapple.

speaker: TERESA
text: You finally kept the limits of what you know.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: LUPE [VOICE NOTE]: I am now a woman of great restraint. But a new message has arrived. Someone says the notice was for apartment nine. Marta lives in six.

speaker: TERESA
text: Don't forward anything. First verify the apartment number and the document.

speaker: SFX
text: Silence. Then an incoming message chime.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: UNKNOWN VOICE [VOICE NOTE]: Hello, Teresa. I'm calling from the clinic simulation. I need to correct something I said this morning. The person didn't say “I never had pain.” They said “I haven't had pain today.” I think someone removed the word *today* in the report.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Teresa looks at the empty space beside her notebook where she has written three words: who, when, maybe. A new fourth word joins them: *today*.

speaker: SFX
text: The radio starts again, playing the same melody in a different key.

speaker: TERESA
text: Lupe, I'm going to need you to stop calling every message a verdict.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: LUPE [VOICE NOTE]: I already changed the group name.

speaker: TERESA
text: To what?

speaker: LUPE
text: “Solo Avisos — Sujeto a Verificación.”

speaker: NARRATOR
text: For once, the group is quiet. Then the typing dots appear. Five people, all at once.

speaker: SFX
text: END EPISODE — THE MISSING DAY
